hook: Your Wi-Fi sneaks through walls, but some walls are tougher!
headline: Your Wi-Fi's Secret Path Through Walls
source: Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Guidelines on Radio Frequency Propagation

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: Walls Block Wi-Fi? 🧱
slides.bubble: My signal is weak in the kitchen! Does Wi-Fi really go through walls?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Invisible Radio Waves 📶
slides.bubble: Yes! Wi-Fi uses radio waves, like tiny invisible signals traveling everywhere.

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: Speed Bump Materials 🚧
slides.bubble: So why is it weaker here? Are some walls like giant speed bumps?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Your Wall's Story? 🤔
slides.bubble: Metal and concrete slow signals most! What's your wall made of? Tell me!

takeaway: Wi-Fi signals are radio waves that pass through walls, but dense materials like metal or concrete weaken them significantly.
